explanations: terra: Abraham asks God to “raise/send among them a messenger” (وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا); it states both sides missing from انْبَعَثَ—a raiser and the one raised—and joins b-ʿ-th to r-s-l.
terra: The verse tests who “follows the messenger” and who turns “upon his two heels” (عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ); it brings the section’s following, messenger, and bodily heel into one moral fork.

luna: The source-section's root `ل ه م` has a secondary dictionary gloss for a young animal nursing at its mother; this ayah directly describes mothers nursing their children and so supplies the human counterpart. | terra: Mothers nurse their children for a complete term, receive provision, and must not be harmed through the child; this human law clarifies the section’s nursing-young detail as a protected relation of body, feeding, and due share.

luna: The source-section's root `ب ع ث` describes both a driver raising a camel and its own rising; here `ثم بعثه` describes the man restored to life by God, and the ayah then directs him to look at his donkey and at bones being reassembled and clothed in flesh, contrasting an externally caused raising with 91:12's camel rising without a raiser. | terra: After causing a man to die for a hundred years, God “then raised him” (ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُ), while the surrounding sign also reconstructs his donkey’s bones; bodily raising and animal body are held together.
terra: Like Pharaoh’s people and those before them, deniers are seized by God “for their sins” (بِذُنُوبِهِمْ); the formula parallels the reason given for Thamud’s crushing.

terra: Zechariah calls his wife barren (عَاقِرٌ); the same Qur’anic root that names the camel’s hock-cut here marks a body unable to bear offspring, adding a reproductive edge to the dam-and-young image.

luna: The source-section identifies `ع ق ب` with the camel's hock and the back of the foot; `على أعقابكم` uses heels for turning back if a messenger dies or is killed, making physical retreat resonate with the community's rejection of Ṣāliḥ's warning. | terra: Muhammad is called a messenger, his possible death or killing is posed, and the hearers may turn “on your heels” (عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ); messenger, killed body, and heel become one warning.

luna: The source-section's root `ع ق ب` names the hock and heel; this ayah warns that following disbelievers can turn people `على أعقابكم`, a bodily image of retreat that reverses obedience to the messenger and his camel command. | terra: The warned believers may be turned back “on your heels” (عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ); it uses ʿaqib in the bodily rear-foot sense supplied by the section’s dictionary note.
terra: God favors believers when He “raised among them a messenger” (بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا); divine agency contrasts with the section’s unexpressed instigator of the worst man’s rising.

terra: After the first human murder, God “sent/raised a crow” (بَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُرَابًا) to work the earth and teach burial; an animal sent after violence reverses the man who rises in order to violate an animal body.

terra: God disowns human-invented livestock categories including the released sāʾiba; this bounds the section’s release imagery by contrasting fabricated sacred-camel rules with the explicit divine right of Allah’s she-camel.

terra: God says earlier generations were destroyed “for their sins” (بِذُنُوبِهِمْ); it repeats the section’s exact causal movement from ذنب to communal destruction while the source dictionary also hears the animal’s rear in the word.
terra: God takes people by night and “raises you in it” by day (يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ) until an appointed term; repeated bodily rising is explicitly caused and measured.
terra: The speaker refuses to be returned “on our heels” (عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِنَا) after divine guidance; the physical rear becomes an image of moral reversal rather than a tendon cut from outside.

terra: Human beings allocate what is in livestock wombs to men, forbid it to wives, and share it if stillborn; these invented rules over female animal bodies contrast with God’s explicit apportionment of the she-camel’s right.

terra: The verse names a pair of camels and asks whether God forbade the males, the females, or what the females’ wombs contain; it directly joins camel sex, maternal body, and offspring while exposing invented restrictions.
terra: The camel’s entering a needle’s eye marks an impossible bodily passage; it shifts the animal from vulnerable female body to a measure of size and an absolute boundary.

terra: Immediately before Salih’s camel scene, God “cut off the last/rear” (قَطَعْنَا دَابِرَ) of sign-deniers; it prefigures the section’s movement from cutting an animal’s rear to erasing a denying people.

luna: The source-section noun/root `ناقة` identifies the same animal: Ṣāliḥ names her as God's sign, permits her to graze, and forbids harm, the boundary the later hamstringing crosses. | terra: Salih identifies “Allah’s she-camel” as a sign, gives her leave to graze in Allah’s land, and forbids harmful touch; this directly supplies the body, pasture, and protected freedom developed in the section.

terra: Immediately after the camel’s grazing right, Thamud is reminded that God settled it in the land and is warned not to spread corruption there; its expansive occupation sharpens the wrong of denying one animal room to graze.

terra: Within the camel episode, the believers affirm that Salih is “sent” (مُرْسَلٌ) by his Lord; this identifies the human messenger behind رَسُولُ اللَّهِ and activates the section’s r-s-l camel diction.
terra: The arrogant answer the believers, “we disbelieve in what you believe,” giving the immediate communal rejection that turns into bodily assault in 7:77.

luna: `فعقروا الناقة` is the same assault; the source-section root `ع ق ر` is glossed there as cutting the camel's hock tendon. | terra: The people hamstring “the she-camel” (فَعَقَرُوا النَّاقَةَ), defy their Lord’s command, and challenge Salih, joining the exact bodily act to rejection of the messenger.

luna: The quake seizes the people immediately after 7:77's hamstringing; this supplies the consequence that the source section says follows the camel's injury. | terra: The quake leaves the camel killers fallen motionless in their homes; their prone bodies reverse the animal they first disabled and enact the consequence announced at the harmful touch.

luna: After the camel's injury and punishment, Ṣāliḥ says he delivered his Lord's message and advised them; this clarifies the messenger's warning role in 91:13. | terra: After the destruction Salih turns away and says he delivered his Lord’s message (رِسَالَةَ رَبِّي); r-s-l remains audible after the camel’s body and her killers are gone.
terra: Moses identifies himself to Pharaoh as a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, setting up the same r-s-l wordplay completed by release in 7:105.
terra: After presenting clear proof, Moses commands Pharaoh to send/release the Children of Israel with him; the verse makes release the messenger’s concrete demand.
terra: Satan recoils “on his two heels” (عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ) when the armies come into view; the named root denotes an enacted backward movement of the foot.
terra: Pharaoh’s people and earlier deniers are seized “for their sins” (بِذُنُوبِهِمْ), with God severe in punishment; the same syntax turns guilt into what follows the transgression.
terra: The verse again says earlier peoples denied signs and were destroyed “for their sins” (بِذُنُوبِهِمْ); sign-denial, guilt, and destruction reproduce the camel episode’s causal chain.

terra: God dislikes the hypocrites’ setting out (انْبِعَاثَهُمْ), restrains them, and they are told to sit; this exact cognate reverses the source dictionary scene of a hobbled camel released and made to rise.
terra: A witness “follows it” (يَتْلُوهُ) from God; this uses t-l-w in the spatial sense named by the source’s calf following its dam, now for testimony following proof.
terra: Salih reminds Thamud that God produced them from the earth and settled them in it; this frames the later command to let Allah’s camel eat in that same divinely granted earth.

luna: This repeats the she-camel as God's sign and the command to let her graze untouched; its ban makes the offense in 11:65 legible. | terra: Salih again presents Allah’s she-camel as a sign, tells his people to let her eat in Allah’s land, and warns that harming her will bring a near punishment.

luna: `فعقروها` names the camel's hamstringing, matching the source-section's specific bodily gloss of root `ع ق ر`. | terra: After “they hamstrung her” (فَعَقَرُوهَا), Salih grants only three days of enjoyment; the verse makes the cut immediately open onto its promised aftermath.

luna: After the camel's violation, God saves Ṣāliḥ and the believers; this supplies the other side of the outcome, distinct from the wrongdoers' fate in 11:67. | terra: When the decree arrives, God saves Salih and the believers by mercy; the verse separates the messenger and hearers of his warning from the consequence following the camel’s injury.

luna: The cry seizes the wrongdoers after 11:65's injury; the verse gives the collective aftermath of the bodily act. | terra: The blast seizes the wrongdoers and leaves them fallen in their dwellings, a bodily reversal immediately following their hamstringing of the camel.

luna: The next verse says it was as though Thamud had never lived there; it gives the scale of the aftermath after the camel's injury and the cry in 11:67. | terra: The fallen people are described as though they had never lived there, and Thamud’s denial of its Lord is named; this closes the bodily aftermath begun in 11:65.

terra: The brothers ask for an added camel-load; because the source itself glosses b-ʿ-th with بَعِير, the ayah offers a specific but indirect view of the camel body as a unit of carrying capacity rather than a body being raised.

terra: The herald promises a camel-load to whoever recovers the cup; the camel is again an implicit bodily measure of burden, a peripheral counterpart to the source’s بَعِير under release and movement.

luna: The source-section links root `ع ق ب` from the camel's hock to what follows an act; here `عقبى الدار` names a good outcome granted for patience, a counter-outcome to Thamud's violation after Ṣāliḥ is told to be patient in 54:27.
terra: The people of al-Hijr, Thamud’s community, deny the messengers; this is a compact parallel to the denial that precedes violence against the camel.
terra: God gives the people His signs and they turn away from them; in the fuller Thamud accounts the she-camel is precisely such a sign.
terra: They carve mountain houses while feeling secure; the apparently protected dwellings make the morning destruction of the camel’s people a bodily and spatial reversal.
terra: The blast seizes them in the morning, supplying another direct continuation from Thamud’s rejected signs to communal punishment.
terra: What Thamud had acquired does not avail it; the verse closes the al-Hijr account by stripping away the security named around its houses.
terra: Livestock carry loads to lands people could reach only with severe hardship; this makes the animal’s body and ease of travel the benefit corresponding to the source’s camel of easy gait.
terra: Rain gives drink and grows vegetation “in which you pasture” (فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ); water and grazing appear as one divine provision behind the she-camel’s linked pasture and water rights.

terra: God “raised/sent in every community a messenger” (بَعَثْنَا ... رَسُولًا) and ends by asking for the عَاقِبَة of the deniers; it joins the section’s rising, messenger, denial, and consequence under an explicit divine agent.

terra: God gives drink from inside livestock bodies, pure milk between waste and blood (نُسْقِيكُمْ ... لَبَنًا خَالِصًا); it joins the section’s suckling young, udder, animal body, and s-q-y provision.

luna: `ثمود الناقة مبصرة` presents the she-camel as a visible sign and says Thamud wronged it; this joins the body's injury to the sign's rejection. | terra: God says He gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign and they wronged her; the surrounding language of sending signs also keeps the camel’s r-s-l association active.
terra: God says “then We raised them” (ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاهُمْ) after the sleepers had lain in the cave; it preserves the section’s two-sided action in which one party causes a resting body to rise.
terra: The sleepers are again said to have been raised so that they question one another; their post-rest movement gives an explicit agent and purpose to b-ʿ-th.
terra: Zechariah says his wife “was barren” (كَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا); against the source section’s ʿaqr of a limb, this root sense places interruption in the line of offspring.
terra: The question repeats that his wife is barren (امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا); the wonder of a promised child reverses the root’s bodily sense of barrenness, relevant to the camel and following young.

terra: Moses and Aaron say they are two messengers of the Lord and command Pharaoh, “send/release with us” (فَأَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا) Israel; messenger and release occur together as in the section’s untethering explanation.
terra: “Eat and pasture your livestock” (وَارْعَوْا أَنْعَامَكُمْ) places human food and animal grazing together within God’s vegetation, matching the protected leave to eat in God’s land.

luna: The section pairs the moon with the sun in a following relation; this ayah says both move in their own orbits, giving the same celestial pair's ordered motion while leaving the section's specific follower relation distinct.

luna: The section's calf follows its mother; `مرضعة عما أرضعت` depicts the opposite boundary, a nursing mother losing awareness of the child at the terrors of the Hour. | terra: The Hour makes every nursing female forget what she nurses and every pregnant female drop her load; this catastrophic severing of mother and young contrasts with the section’s calf following and feeding from its dam.
terra: Pilgrims come on every lean mount from distant passes; the journey-worn camel body and sustained gait give a Qur’anic scene for the source’s easy-moving camel.

luna: The source-section distinguishes cutting the sign-camel's hock from the later lexical use of `ع ق ر` for slaughter at the throat; 22:36 describes sacrificial camels whose fallen sides become food to share, a distinct camel's bodily fate. | terra: Sacrificial camel bodies are made among God’s rites, lined up for His name and eaten only after their sides fall; this supplies the lawful, God-directed boundary against attacking Allah’s protected she-camel.

terra: Livestock are a lesson because God gives drink from what is in their bellies (نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهَا); the animal body itself becomes the source of the watering named beside the she-camel.
terra: God’s signs were “recited” (تُتْلَىٰ) to them, yet they retreated “on your heels” (عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِكُمْ); both named roots shift from recitation to bodily rearward motion in one verse.
terra: Moses and Aaron are to tell Pharaoh that they are a messenger of the Lord of the worlds; this supplies the r-s-l office whose requested release follows in 26:17.
terra: The messengers command Pharaoh to “send/release with us” the Children of Israel; it repeats the section’s relation between messenger and the act of letting a restrained party go.

luna: `كذبت ثمود المرسلين` opens another account of the same community rejecting its messengers, matching the rejection of the messenger who names the camel in 91:13–14. | terra: “Thamud denied the messengers” (كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ); the collective formula explains the section’s فَكَذَّبُوهُ as rejection of the messenger whose warning protects the camel.
luna: Ṣāliḥ asks whether they will fear God; this introduces the warning stance before 26:143 names him as messenger and 26:155–156 give the camel command.

luna: Ṣāliḥ calls himself a trustworthy `رسول`; the source-section root `ر س ل` also describes an easy-moving camel, and 26:155–156 give this messenger's specific camel and water warning. | terra: Salih says, “I am to you a trustworthy messenger” (رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ), giving the same speaker and r-s-l title that the section hears against the easy gait of the camel.
luna: Ṣāliḥ commands them to fear God and obey him; 26:155–156 specify the camel-care command that the community violates.
terra: The Thamud passage places the people amid gardens and springs; their abundant water makes resistance to the she-camel’s single allotted drink especially pointed.
terra: Crops and palms heavy with fruit complete the provision surrounding Thamud; this is the edible landscape in which they deny the camel her measured share.
luna: Ṣāliḥ repeats “fear God and obey me” just before describing the camel; this frames the camel's protection as part of the command they reject.
luna: He forbids obedience to the extravagant, which sharpens the opposition between his camel warning and the transgressive act in 26:157; 26:155–156 state the warning itself.
luna: Those he warns against are described as spreading corruption and not setting things right; their treatment of the protected camel in 26:155–157 makes that description concrete.
luna: The people answer Ṣāliḥ's warning by calling him bewitched; this is their resistance before he presents the camel in 26:155.

luna: They demand a sign from Ṣāliḥ, which the following 26:155 identifies as the camel; this ayah supplies the challenge to which the camel responds. | terra: Thamud demands a sign from Salih if he is truthful; the she-camel of 26:155 is therefore not incidental livestock but the answer whose body they then test.

luna: `هذه ناقة لها شرب ولكم شرب يوم معلوم` gives the camel and people separate allotted drinking turns, matching the source-section's `س ق ي` / watering detail. | terra: Salih assigns the she-camel her own drink (لَهَا شِرْبٌ) and the people theirs on a known day, spelling out the watering right compressed into سُقْيَاهَا.

luna: The warning `ولا تمسوها بسوء` draws a boundary around the camel before 26:157 recounts the hamstringing; this ayah contributes the explicit prohibition and threatened consequence. | terra: Salih forbids touching the camel with harm and warns of a tremendous day’s punishment; it marks the protected boundary her body is made to cross in 26:157.

luna: `فعقروها` repeats the hamstringing and adds that they became remorseful; the root `ع ق ر` keeps the act located in the camel's body. | terra: “They hamstrung her” (فَعَقَرُوهَا) and awoke remorseful; the exact act is followed first by inward consequence, before the punishment in 26:158.

luna: `فأخذهم العذاب` follows the camel's killing in 26:157, supplying the punishment after the offense that the source section's sequence anticipates. | terra: The punishment seizes them and the verse calls the episode a sign; it completes the sequence from demanded sign, to wounded camel, to communal consequence.
luna: The closing words call the episode a sign; its own contribution is to frame the camel's fate and punishment as a warning, with 26:155–158 giving the specific events.
terra: God says He “sent” Salih to Thamud (أَرْسَلْنَا ... صَالِحًا), after which the people split into contending parties; it supplies the r-s-l agency and divided audience behind the camel warning.
terra: The same Thamud account identifies nine men spreading corruption; without equating them with the cutter, it sets the section’s single worst actor inside an organized corrupt collective.
terra: In the Salih narrative God commands attention to “the aftermath of their plot” (عَاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ) and says He destroyed them all; it gives the named ع-q-b consequence a collective object.
terra: Their houses stand ruined because of their wrongdoing; it makes the aftermath in 27:51 visible in the very dwellings from which the camel’s communal enemies acted.
terra: God saves those who believed and were mindful; the surviving group marks the boundary within the people whose destruction follows the crime.
luna: The source-section's root `ل ه م` has a secondary dictionary gloss for a young animal taking milk at its mother's teat; `أرضعيه` gives a human mother nursing Moses, a specific nursing parallel.
terra: Moses finds a whole people watering their flocks while two women hold theirs back; this stages the animal-watering access and restraint implicit in the camel’s allotted drink.
terra: Moses waters the women’s animals for them (فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا), completing the herd-and-water scene opened in 28:23 and supplying a benevolent human agent of s-q-y.
terra: “Each We seized for his sin” (فَكُلًّا أَخَذْنَا بِذَنْبِهِ) introduces several bodily forms of destruction, clarifying how a single named guilt can issue in a whole people’s fate.

luna: The section casts the moon as the sun's follower (source-section root ت ل و); `لا الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر` sets their order by saying the sun does not overtake the moon. | terra: The sun may not overtake the moon, nor night outstrip day, and each moves in an orbit; this sets a cosmic boundary around the section’s picture of the moon following the sun like a calf following its dam.

luna: `من بعثنا من مرقدنا` uses the source-section root `ب ع ث` for people awakened at resurrection; it contrasts the camel's ordinary arising in 91:12 with a raising that requires an agent. | terra: The resurrected ask who “raised us from our resting place” (بَعَثَنَا مِن مَرْقَدِنَا), then acknowledge the messengers; unlike the uncaused-looking انْبَعَثَ in the section, this rising explicitly seeks its raiser.

terra: Subdued livestock provide benefits and drinks (مَشَارِبُ); the question “will they not give thanks?” casts animal provision as a trust, illuminating Thamud’s refusal to honor one animal’s drink.

terra: Solomon’s action concerns horses’ shins and necks (بِالسُّوقِ وَالْأَعْنَاقِ), but whether مَسْحًا means stroking or striking is disputed; either reading makes an uncertain yet specific animal-body counterpart to the camel’s hock and later throat.

luna: The section's moon-after-sun sequence belongs to a larger ordered cycle; `يكور الليل على النهار` and the sun and moon running to appointed terms show the paired bodies and day-night succession around it.
terra: Former peoples stronger in force and monuments are seized “for their sins” (بِذُنُوبِهِمْ); power does not shield bodies from the consequence attached to guilt.

luna: The she-camel is a visible sign in 17:59; this account says Thamud preferred blindness over guidance and were struck for it, making their refusal of the sign a specific reversal of its visibility. | terra: Thamud is shown guidance but prefers blindness, so the humiliating thunderbolt seizes it for what it earned; this states the chosen moral movement behind the hand that attacks the camel.
terra: God saves those who believe and are mindful, separating them from the Thamud body seized in 41:17 just as other camel accounts save Salih and his hearers.
terra: Thamud is told to enjoy itself “until a time,” echoing the short respite announced after the camel is hamstrung in 11:65.
terra: They defy their Lord’s command and the thunderbolt seizes them while they look on; it supplies the disobedience and seizure that lead to their inability to stand in 51:45.

luna: The camel in the source section rises without a handler, while this ayah says Thamud could not rise or defend themselves after punishment; 51:44 supplies the preceding disobedience and thunderbolt, and this verse contributes their helplessness. | terra: After Thamud’s defiance and thunderbolt, “they were unable to rise” (فَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا مِنْ قِيَامٍ); the people’s final incapacity reverses the worst man’s rising toward the camel.

luna: `كذبت ثمود بالنذر` states the community's rejection of warnings, the stance that leads into Ṣāliḥ's camel warning and their denial of him in the source section. | terra: “Thamud denied the warnings” opens the compact camel account; it identifies the collective denial that 54:29 concentrates in one companion’s hand.

luna: The people object to following one mortal from among them; this gives their resistance to Ṣāliḥ's warning, while 54:27 identifies the camel test at issue. | terra: Thamud asks whether it should “follow” (نَتَّبِعُهُ) one human from among them; inside the camel story, their refusal to follow the messenger reverses the section’s young camel naturally following its dam.

luna: Their question about the reminder and accusation that he is a liar anticipates 91:14's denial of the messenger; 54:27 then makes the warning concrete through the camel. | terra: The people reject the reminder’s being cast upon one man among them and call him a liar; their attack on the selected recipient precedes the divinely selected camel in 54:27.

luna: The promised exposure of the liar and insolent anticipates the consequence after the camel test in 54:27–31; this ayah contributes the forecast before that sequence. | terra: They are told that tomorrow they will know who is the insolent liar; the promised near disclosure begins the temporal aftermath that the hock-cut triggers.

luna: `إنا مرسلو الناقة فتنة لهم` sends the she-camel as a test; the source-section root `ر س ل` links the messenger's name with the camel's easy movement, while this verse makes sending her the trial. | terra: God says He is “sending the she-camel” (مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ) as a trial; the camel and the r-s-l word meet explicitly, while God supplies the agent behind its release.

luna: The water is divided between them and each drinking turn is attended; this is the same camel-water arrangement named by `وسقياها` in the source section. | terra: God orders Salih to announce that the water is divided between them and that each drinking turn must be attended; it completes the trial announced in 54:27.

luna: After they call their companion, `فتعاطى فعقر` singles out the agent who takes up the act; it matches the source-section's lone wretched man and root `ع ق ر`. | terra: The group calls its companion, who reaches out and hamstrings (فَعَقَرَ); this is the fullest parallel to the section’s one rising culprit acting for the collective.

luna: This asks how severe God's punishment and warning were, directly interpreting the camel episode and the cry that follows it in 54:31. | terra: The question “How were My punishment and warnings?” places the communal stroke directly after the single man’s stroke against the camel.

luna: The single cry comes after the companion hamstrings the camel in 54:29; it completes this retelling's consequence. | terra: A single blast leaves them like the dry debris of an enclosure (هِشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ); the camel trial ends with its keepers reduced to the wreckage of an animal pen.
terra: The condemned drink “like the drinking of thirsty camels” (شُرْبَ الْهِيمِ); uncontrolled thirst reverses the she-camel’s measured, protected drinking turn.
terra: God is the one who “raised among the unlettered a messenger” (بَعَثَ ... رَسُولًا); the b-ʿ-th and r-s-l camel-derived associations meet in their ordinary Qur’anic mission sense.
luna: The source-section's root `ل ه م` has a secondary dictionary gloss for a young animal at its mother's teat; this ayah describes mothers nursing children and the care owed for that act.
terra: Thamud is said to have denied the Striking Calamity; the terse statement joins its denial to the catastrophe specified in 69:5.
terra: Thamud is destroyed by the overwhelming blast, adding a concise formulation of what follows the camel crime even though the animal is not named here.
luna: The moon follows the sun in the section's ordered sky, while `وجمع الشمس والقمر` brings the same pair together at the Last Hour, a specific reversal of their ordinary relation.

terra: The oath by “those sent forth” uses a feminine plural of r-s-l and depicts ordered release or motion, but the referents are disputed; it is therefore only an uncertain lexical echo of the source’s easily dispatched مَرَاسِيل camels.
terra: Hell’s sparks are compared to yellow camels; the simile turns the familiar mass and motion of camel bodies into fire, an opposite use of the section’s living female animal.
terra: God brings from the earth “its water and its pasture” (مَاءَهَا وَمَرْعَاهَا); the pair names the two provisions assigned to the she-camel.
terra: The water and pasture are provision “for you and your livestock,” making humans and animals joint beneficiaries rather than rivals over the share.
terra: Among the foods God grows are fruit and pasture (أَبًّا); the latter supplies the animal side of the earth from which the she-camel is told to eat.
terra: The growth is provision “for you and your livestock,” again setting human and herd within one apportioned gift.

terra: At the final upheaval, valuable pregnant she-camels are left unattended (الْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ); abandonment reverses the section’s ordinary chain of dam, following young, pasture, and scheduled water.

terra: The murdered girl is asked “for what sin” (بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ); an innocent female body and ذنب are separated, exposing the guilt of those who kill, as the she-camel’s killers are crushed بِذَنْبِهِمْ.
luna: The section calls the camel's attacker `أشقاها`; here `ويتجنبها الأشقى` applies “most wretched” to the one who avoids the reminder, tying that label to rejection of warning.
terra: “Do they not look at the camels, how they were created?” directs attention to the camel’s made body, the very body whose gait, joints, udder, hock, heel, and rear the section anatomizes.
luna: `الأشقى` again names the one who reaches the great Fire, extending the source section's label for the camel's attacker toward an outcome; 92:16 specifies his denial and turning away.

luna: This identifies the wretched one as `الذي كذب وتولى`, a denial-and-turning-away pattern that clarifies the source section's statement that Thamud rejected Ṣāliḥ before attacking the sign; 92:15 gives the stated Fire outcome.

terra: The command “sacrifice” (وَانْحَرْ) supplies the nahr named in the source definition, distinguishing throat-slaughter offered to God from the forbidden hock-cut that the definition says later lent it the name ʿaqr.
